title: Strict point transport on simultaneous quotient complexes
statement:
Fix the finite-field datum $p,a,q,k_0,k$, a prime $\ell\ne p$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, its valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$, a uniformizer $\varpi$, and $A_n=\mathcal O_E/\varpi^n$ for $n\ge1$ [def-trf-coefficient-conventions]. Put $s=\operatorname{Spec}k$, $g=\operatorname{Spec}(\gamma)$ for geometric Frobenius [def-weil-frobenius-detailed], $R=\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,s}=\lim_n(A_n)_s$, and $\Gamma=\Gamma(s,-)$ on the small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site, def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients, lem-weil-point-proetale-sections-exact]. For a flat-term K-flat complex $P$ of $R$-modules [def-pc-kflat-complex, def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules], put $P_n=P\otimes_R(A_n)_s$, $r_n(x)=x\otimes1$, and $t_n=1\otimes(A_{n+1}\to A_n)$ [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum]. Let $C_n=\operatorname{Res}_ng_n^*P_n$, with the coefficient-induced transition $v_n:C_{n+1}\to C_n$ of [def-weil-inverse-image-pullback-comparison](b); put $D_n=\Gamma P_n$, $B_n=\Gamma C_n$. All these towers are over the single integral coefficient ring after restriction of scalars. Use the restriction/colimit-insertion/sheafification map $\sigma$ and finite tensor-insertion comparison $\kappa$ of [def-weil-frobenius-point-transport, def-weil-inverse-image-pullback-comparison]. The maps $u_n=\Gamma(\kappa_{P_n})\sigma_{P_n}:D_n\to B_n$ are $\mathcal O_E$-linear chain maps satisfying the strict equalities
$$\Gamma(v_n)u_{n+1}=u_n\Gamma(t_n),\qquad \Gamma(\theta_n)\sigma_P=u_n\Gamma(r_n),\qquad \theta_n=\kappa_{P_n}g^{-1}(r_n).$$
They therefore give a strict tower map $u(P):D_\bullet\to B_\bullet$. The equalities use the actual quotient coefficient maps and the structure square $\pi_nc_{\mathcal O_E}=c_{A_n}g^{-1}(\pi_n)$; they hold before localization. For every chain map $f:P\to P'$ between such complexes, writing $f_n=f\otimes1$, one has
$$u_n(P')\Gamma(f_n)=\Gamma(g_n^*f_n)u_n(P).$$
The two tower functors and this map descend through quasi-isomorphisms between flat-term K-flat representatives to a natural transformation on the derived category of $R$-modules, independently of the common representative. Its source is sections of the coherent reduction tower and its target is sections of the finite pullback quotient tower. If $N=[P]$ lies in $D^b_c(s,\mathcal O_E)$ [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed], its $n$-th evaluation is precisely $\iota_{N_n}$, where $N_n=N\otimes_R^L(A_n)_s$.

source.place: clause (3), simultaneous quotient transport: original realization proof steps 1-2 and chain/tower naturality in step 6

proof.text:
Put $S_n=(A_n)_s$ and $\rho_n:S_{n+1}\to S_n$. Use the same inverse-image functor on underlying abelian sheaves at every coefficient level. Apply [lem-weil-point-automorphism-restriction-natural] to $g=\operatorname{Spec}(\gamma)$ with $\Lambda=\mathcal O_E$, on $P$ and on each $P_n$ restricted along $\pi_n:R\to S_n$. It gives $\mathcal O_E$-linear chain maps $\sigma$ and strict naturality for $r_n,t_n$ and $f_n$. These are the specified restriction/colimit-insertion/sheafification maps, since their underlying construction does not change with the coefficient ring. In [def-weil-inverse-image-pullback-comparison](a), write $j_n=\kappa_{P_n}$ for the actual sheafified tensor insertion. It is a chain map. It is $R$-linear with the transported integral action on its source: for a local section $a$ of $R$ and $x$ of $g^{-1}P_n$, the square $\pi_nc_{\mathcal O_E}=c_{A_n}g^{-1}(\pi_n)$ gives
$$j_n(c_{\mathcal O_E}^{-1}(a)x)=x\otimes\pi_n(a)=a\,j_n(x).$$
Consequently $u_n=\Gamma(j_n)\sigma_{P_n}$ is an $\mathcal O_E$-linear chain map. This uses no completeness or boundedness assumption on $P$.

source.place: clause (3), simultaneous quotient transport; explicit restriction map and structure square of comparison (a),(b)

proof.text:
The coefficient-defined map $v_n$ of [def-weil-inverse-image-pullback-comparison](b) is induced on the presheaf tensor by $x\otimes b\mapsto g^{-1}(t_n)(x)\otimes\rho_n(b)$. Its balancing relation is respected because $\rho_n c_{A_{n+1}}=c_{A_n}g^{-1}(\rho_n)$ by [lem-weil-proetale-isomorphism-inverse-image](3). Thus, on $x\in g^{-1}P_{n+1}(U)$, both $v_nj_{n+1}$ and $j_ng^{-1}(t_n)$ send $x$ to $g^{-1}(t_n)(x)\otimes1$. Their composites with the sheafification unit are equal, so
$$v_nj_{n+1}=j_ng^{-1}(t_n).$$
Here we used the actual tensor product of [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product], not an identification between independently chosen derived reductions. The calculation is degreewise and respects every restriction map.

source.place: Tag 03EK, section-tensor-product; Tag 03D6, definition-pushforward, pullback clause; coefficient-induced transition of comparison (b)

proof.text:
Naturality of $\sigma$ in [lem-weil-point-automorphism-restriction-natural], applied to the $R$-linear chain map $t_n:P_{n+1}\to P_n$, gives $\Gamma(g^{-1}t_n)\sigma_{P_{n+1}}=\sigma_{P_n}\Gamma(t_n)$. Combining with Step 2 yields
$$\Gamma(v_n)u_{n+1}=\Gamma(j_ng^{-1}t_n)\sigma_{P_{n+1}}=\Gamma(j_n)\sigma_{P_n}\Gamma(t_n)=u_n\Gamma(t_n).$$
By [def-weil-inverse-system] these equations make $u(P)$ a strict map of towers, already in complexes over $\mathcal O_E$.

source.place: clause (3), compatibility with all quotient transitions before localization

proof.text:
By [def-weil-inverse-image-pullback-comparison](b), $\theta_n=j_ng^{-1}(r_n)$. Apply the same strict naturality of [lem-weil-point-automorphism-restriction-natural] to $r_n:P\to P_n$, regarded as an $R$-linear chain map. Then
$$\Gamma(\theta_n)\sigma_P=\Gamma(j_n)\Gamma(g^{-1}r_n)\sigma_P=\Gamma(j_n)\sigma_{P_n}\Gamma(r_n)=u_n\Gamma(r_n).$$
The scalar action on this equation is the one verified in Step 1 by the structure square; no inverse of a quotient map is used.

source.place: clause (3), compatibility with the quotient augmentations in comparison (b)

proof.text:
For a chain map $f:P\to P'$, the maps $f_n=f\otimes1$ commute with $t_n$ by the tensor formula, and their pullbacks commute with $v_n$ by the formula in Step 2. Tensor insertion satisfies the strict sheaf-map equality $(g_n^*f_n)j_n(P)=j_n(P')g^{-1}(f_n)$: on a section $x$ both sides are $g^{-1}(f_n)(x)\otimes1$, followed by sheafification [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product, def-weil-inverse-image-pullback-comparison]. Naturality of $\sigma$ [lem-weil-point-automorphism-restriction-natural] now gives
$$\Gamma(g_n^*f_n)u_n(P)=\Gamma(j_n(P'))\Gamma(g^{-1}f_n)\sigma_{P_n}=u_n(P')\Gamma(f_n).$$
Functoriality of the termwise constructions and these two tower compatibilities make $D(P)$ and $B(P)$ functors on the flat-term K-flat complexes and $u$ a natural transformation between them.

source.place: clause (3), chain-map naturality of simultaneous quotient transport

proof.text: If $f:P\to P'$ is a quasi-isomorphism between the indicated K-flat complexes, [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings](1), applied to $R\to S_n$, says $f_n$ is a quasi-isomorphism, even though $S_n$ need not be flat over $R$. At finite level the inverse image and module pullback in [def-weil-inverse-image-pullback-comparison](a) are exact for this scheme automorphism; hence $g_n^*f_n$ is a quasi-isomorphism. Restriction of scalars changes only the action [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars], so kernels and cokernels have the same underlying abelian sheaves and quasi-isomorphisms remain quasi-isomorphisms. Exact sections [lem-weil-point-proetale-sections-exact] therefore send both maps to quasi-isomorphisms. Thus both strict tower functors take $f$ to a levelwise quasi-isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 06YT, lemma-derived-tor-quasi-isomorphism-other-side; Tag 06YY, lemma-derived-base-change; exact sections at the geometric point

proof.text: Take as target $\mathcal T=D(\operatorname{Fun}(\mathbf Z_{\ge1}^{\mathrm{op}},\operatorname{Mod}(\mathcal O_E)))$: a strict tower of complexes is a complex of towers, and its quasi-isomorphisms are exactly the levelwise ones. The required abelian diagram category exists by [lem-weil-pbc-small-module-diagrams-grothendieck], applied to the one-object trivial site with ring $\mathcal O_E$ and the small tower index. Kernels and cokernels are pointwise: take the kernels or cokernels at every level and use the commuting transition squares to induce their transitions; their universal properties are checked levelwise. Use the derived category of [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. If $f-f'=dh+hd$, apply tensor, inverse image and sections termwise to $h$ as well. This produces homotopies $\Gamma(h\otimes1)$ for $D$ and $\Gamma(g_n^*(h\otimes1))$ for $B$. Their components commute with transitions by the same tensor formulas as in Step 5. Thus they are homotopies in complexes of towers, and the two functors in Step 5, after target localization, factor through the homotopy category of flat-term K-flat complexes. Their natural transformation does also.

source.place: Tags 05RR and 05RU, derived category; homotopies under additive termwise functors, with the explicit quotient transitions

proof.text:
By [lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent], the homotopy category of K-flat $R$-complexes with flat terms, localized at its quasi-isomorphisms, is equivalent to $D(R)$. The pro-etale site is taken in the small skeleton and containing universe fixed in the statement. Step 6 says the two functors of Step 7 invert these quasi-isomorphisms. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property](1),(2) to obtain the two functors $D(R)\to\mathcal T$ and their natural transformation; its uniqueness clause gives compatibility with the comparison for every other flat-term K-flat representative. Explicitly, naturality $B(a)u(Q)=u(P)D(a)$ for a quasi-isomorphism $a:Q\to P$ implies
$$B(a)^{-1}u(P)=u(Q)D(a)^{-1}.$$
Composing this with $B(b)u(Q)=u(P')D(b)$ proves naturality for a roof $P\xleftarrow{a}Q\xrightarrow{b}P'$; the localization property ensures independence of roof presentation and of representative. The construction retains the strict quotient towers before localization, rather than choosing each level separately.

source.place: Tags 06YS, lemma-K-flat-resolution, and 0G7D, lemma-factor-through-K-flat; resolving-class localization; natural-transformation universal property of localization

proof.text: The $n$-th source evaluation is $\Gamma(P\otimes_RS_n)$, representing sections of $N\otimes_R^LS_n$ by [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings](2). Its transitions and augmentations are exactly those of [def-weil-integral-reduction-tower]. By [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum], applied with $A=\mathcal O_E$, $I=(\varpi)$, so that $A_s=R$ and $(A/I^n)_s=S_n$, the coherent reduction tower of $N$ is the class in $D(\operatorname{Tow}_{\mathcal O_E}(s))$ of the strict tower $F(P)_n=P\otimes_RS_n$ with transitions $1\otimes\rho_n=t_n$, computed on the flat-term K-flat representative $P$ itself; applying the exact functor $\Gamma$ levelwise gives the tower $D_\bullet(P)$, so the descended source functor of Step 8 is sections of the coherent reduction tower. The target evaluation is sections of the corresponding finite module pullback of that same quotient complex, as specified in [def-weil-inverse-image-pullback-comparison](a),(b). If $N=[P]\in D^b_c(s,\mathcal O_E)$, [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed] says $N_n=N\otimes_R^LS_n$ is bounded constructible at finite coefficients. At that level [def-weil-frobenius-point-transport] defines $\iota_{N_n}$ as the class of $\Gamma(j_n)\sigma_{P_n}$, which is exactly $u_n(P)$. Step 8 gives this equality independently of the representative. This proves the last clause and identifies the two descended tower functors as claimed.
